Q16587373.label: National Unity Party
Q16587373.summary: The National Unity Party is a far-right political party in Haiti. It was the de facto sole legal political party under the Duvalier family, the autocratic family dictatorship of François "Papa Doc" Duvalier and his son Jean-Claude "Baby Doc" Duvalier, which lasted from 1957 to 1986.

Q887405.label: Hérard Abraham
Q887405.summary: Hérard Abraham was a Haitian military officer and politician who served as acting President of Haiti between 10 March 1990 and 13 March 1990.

Q3587181.label: 1972 Jamaican general election
Q3587181.summary: General elections were held in Jamaica on 29 February 1972. The result was a victory for the People's National Party, which won 37 of the 53 seats. Voter turnout was 79%.

Q5174893.label: 1948 Costa Rican Constituent Assembly election
Q5174893.summary: Constituent Assembly elections were held in Costa Rica on 8 December 1948, following the Costa Rican Civil War. The elections were convened by the Founding Junta of the Second Republic, which was exercising provisional governmental authority in accordance with the Ulate–Figueres Pact. A total of 45 constituent deputies and 15 alternate members were to be elected.

mentions.c: Costa Rica: 1948 Costa Rican Constituent Assembly election

Q211565.label: 1981 Belgian general election
Q211565.summary: General elections were held in Belgium on 8 November 1981. Voter turnout was 94.5% in the Chamber election and 94.6% in the Senate election. Elections were also held for the nine provincial councils and for the Council of the German Cultural Community. They were the first elections after the voting age was lowered from 21 to 18.

Q15981.label: Robert Schuman
Q15981.summary: Jean-Baptiste Nicolas Robert Schuman was a Luxembourg-born French statesman. Schuman was a Christian democratic political thinker and activist. Twice Prime Minister of France, a reformist Minister of Finance and a Foreign Minister, he was instrumental in building postwar European and trans-Atlantic institutions and was one of the founders of the European Communities, the Council of Europe and NATO. He was the one who proposed the Schuman Declaration, which established the European Coal and Steel Community, ultimately a predecessor of the European Union.

Positions held: Deputy of the French Third Republic
Minister of the Economy, Finances and Industry

Q2075757.label: 1928 French legislative election
Q2075757.summary: Legislative elections were held in France on 22 and 29 April 1928. These elections saw the restoration of the two-round system that had been abolished in 1919.

Q156781.label: Mário Soares
Q156781.summary: Mário Alberto Nobre Lopes Soares was a Portuguese statesman who served as prime minister of Portugal from 1976 to 1978 and from 1983 to 1985 and subsequently as the president of Portugal from 1986 to 1996. He was the first secretary-general of the Socialist Party, from its foundation in 1973 to 1986.

Q55917.desc: 13th Prime Minister of the Republic of Poland
Q55917.summary: Jarosław Aleksander Kaczyński is a Polish politician. He co-founded the Law and Justice (PiS) party in 2001 with his twin brother, Lech Kaczyński, and has served as its leader since 2003.

Q24173.label: 1996 Czech legislative election
Q24173.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in the Czech Republic on 31 May and 1 June 1996, the first after independence. The Civic Democratic Party remained the largest party in the Chamber of Deputies, winning 68 of the 200 seats. Voter turnout was 76%.

Q515693.label: Theodoros Pangalos
Q515693.summary: Theodoros Pangalos was a Greek general, politician and dictator, who ruled Greece from 24 June 1925 to 22 August 1926. A distinguished staff officer and an ardent Venizelist and anti-royalist, Pangalos participated in the Goudi coup in 1909, served with distinction in the Balkan Wars, Macedonian front of World War I, and the Greco-Turkish War (1919–1922), and played a leading role in the September 1922 revolt that deposed King Constantine I and in the establishment of the Second Hellenic Republic.

Q9378925.desc: legislative election in the Soviet Union
Q9378925.summary: Supreme Soviet elections were held in the Soviet Union on 12 June 1966.

Q81517.label: Order and Justice
Q81517.summary: Order and Justice, formerly the Liberal Democratic Party was a right-wing political party in Lithuania that self-identified as "left-of-centre", at least on economic matters. It had eight members in the Seimas, the unicameral Lithuanian parliament, as of the last election it participated in (2016).

Member of: Alliance for Direct Democracy in Europe

Q5450861.label: 1950 Finnish presidential election
Q5450861.summary: Two-stage presidential elections were held in Finland in 1950, the first time the public had been involved in a presidential election since 1937 as three non-popular elections had taken place in 1940, 1943 and 1946. On 16 and 17 January the public elected presidential electors to an electoral college. They in turn elected the President. The result was a victory for Juho Kusti Paasikivi, who won on the first ballot. The turnout for the popular vote was 63.8%. President Paasikivi was at first reluctant to seek re-election, at least in regular presidential elections.

Q125988461.label: 2024 Democratic Republic of the Congo coup attempt
Q125988461.wiki: 2024 Democratic Republic of the Congo coup attempt
Q125988461.summary: On 19 May 2024, an attempted coup d'état took place in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Targeting President Félix Tshisekedi and his Economy Minister Vital Kamerhe, the assailants attacked both the Palais de la Nation and Kamerhe's residence. They were heavily armed and put up an intense fight at the Kamerhe home.

mentions.c: Democratic Republic of the Congo: Coup: 2024 Democratic Republic of the Congo coup attempt

Q714349.label: Rotterdam Blitz
Q714349.desc: aerial bombardment of Rotterdam by the Luftwaffe (German air force) on 14 May 1940, during the German invasion of the Netherlands in World War II
Q714349.img: Rotterdam, Laurenskerk, na bombardement van mei 1940.jpg
Q714349.summary: In 1940, Rotterdam was subjected to heavy aerial bombardment by the Luftwaffe during the German invasion of the Netherlands during the Second World War. The objective was to support the German troops fighting in the city, break Dutch resistance and force the Dutch army to surrender. Bombing began at the outset of hostilities on 10 May and culminated with the destruction of the entire historic city centre on 14 May, an event sometimes referred to as the Rotterdam Blitz.

Q4671597.label: Battle of Palmyra
Q4671597.desc: battle in Syria during the Syria-Lebanon campaign in World War II

Q562797.label: Ostrogozhsk–Rossosh Offensive
Q562797.summary: The Ostrogozhsk–Rossosh offensive was an offensive of the Voronezh Front on the Eastern Front of World War II against the Hungarian 2nd Army and parts of the Italian 8th Army as part of the Voronezh–Kharkov offensive.

Q2525805.label: Zhitomir–Berdichev Offensive
Q2525805.desc: 1943 battle on the Eastern Front of WW2
Q2525805.summary: The Zhitomir–Berdichev offensive, known on the German side as the Defensive battle at Zhitomir and Berdichev, was part of the strategic offensive of the Red Army in the right-bank Ukraine, the Dnieper–Carpathian offensive. The successful offensive operation was conducted by the forces of the 1st Ukrainian Front commanded by General of Army Nikolai Vatutin during World War II, from 24 December 1943 through to 14 January 1944.

Q5016173.label: Cactus Ridge
Q5016173.img: Through the Outposts- XXIV Corps, 4-8 April 1945.jpg
Q5016173.summary: In the Battle of Okinawa, Cactus Ridge was the name U.S. forces gave to a rise of land approximately 600 yards (550 m) southeast of Mashiki, Okinawa which commanded much of the ground between Uchitomari and Oyama, both of which lie along Highway No. 1. The defense of Cactus Ridge to the west, and The Pinnacle to the east, marked the start of resistance by Japanese land forces on Okinawa.

Q3501165.label: Battle of Odžak
Q3501165.desc: 1945 final battle of World War II in Europe
Q3501165.summary: The Battle of Odžak was the last battle of World War II in Europe. The battle began on 19 April 1945 and lasted until 25 May 1945, 17 days after the end of the war in Europe. The combatants were the Axis-aligned Croatian Armed Forces, commanded by Petar Rajkovačić, and the Yugoslav Partisans, commanded by Miloš Zekić. The battle took place in the Bosnian town of Odžak, in the former country of Yugoslavia. The battle was a victory for the partisans.

Q2887789.label: Abagana ambush
Q2887789.summary: The Abagana Ambush was an ambush during the Nigerian Civil War by Biafran troops led by Major Jonathan Uchendu that wiped out the Nigerian 2nd Division. Of the 6,000 Nigerian troops ambushed, only a very small number survived, including the 2nd Division's commander, General Murtala Muhammed.

Q7096941.label: Operation Crescent Wind
Q7096941.summary: Operation Crescent Wind was the codename for the American and British air campaign over Afghanistan from 7 October to 17 December 2001. The bombing campaign was aided by British special forces troops on the ground to provide targeting information for airstrikes.

Q19428973.label: Al-Hasakah offensive
Q19428973.summary: The Eastern Hasakah offensive was launched in the Hasakah Governorate during the Syrian Civil War, by the Kurdish-majority People's Protection Units, Assyrian militias, and allied Arab forces against the jihadist Islamic State, with the intent of retaking the areas of the Jazira Canton that had been captured by ISIL. Subsequently, the Syrian Armed Forces also launched an assault against the jihadists, without coordinating with the YPG.

Q107242093.label: Kola Tembien February 2021 massacres
Q107242093.summary: The February 2021 Kola Tembien massacre was a mass extrajudicial killing that took place in Kola Tembien in the Tigray Region of Ethiopia during the Tigray War, on 10 February 2021. Kola Tembien is a district that belongs to the Central zone of Tigray.

Q111345773.label: Retroville bombing
Q111345773.desc: bombing of a shopping and business centre in Kyiv, Ukraine
Q111345773.img: Shopping center in Kyiv (Podilskyi District) after shelling on 20 March 2022 (02).jpg
Q111345773.summary: On 20 March 2022 around 10:45 pm, the Retroville, a shopping centre located in Kyiv, Ukraine, was bombed in a Russian airstrike. Part of the mall along with its 12-storey business center were destroyed. At least eight people were killed, six of whom were dressed in military fatigues, and one of whom was Russian journalist Oksana Baulina. According to the Russian government, the shopping centre was used as a cover to store and reload ammunition, including the BM-21 Grad multiple rocket launchers by Ukraine.

mentions.c: Part of Russian invasion of Ukraine; 8 deaths

Q126416493.label: Operation Arnon
Q126416493.desc: 2024 Israeli sucessful rescue operation to save four hostages alive from Hamas captivity during the ongoing war in Gaza. Military activity that is also widely accused for being a raid and mass killings of Palestinians

Q597613.label: Ed Case
Q597613.summary: Edward Espenett Case is an American lawyer and politician. A member of the Democratic Party, he has served as the U.S. representative for Hawaii's 1st congressional district since 2019, which covers the urban core of Honolulu. He represented the 2nd district, which covers the rest of the state, from 2002 to 2007.

Positions held: member of the Hawaii House of Representatives

Q47213.label: Warren Buffett
Q47213.summary: Warren Edward Buffett is an American investor and philanthropist who is the chairman emeritus and former CEO of the conglomerate Berkshire Hathaway. As a result of his success, Buffett is one of the best-known investors in the world. According to Forbes, as of January 2026, Buffett's estimated net worth stood at US$148.9 billion, making him the ninth-richest person in the world.

Q8813.label: Bolivarianism
Q8813.summary: Bolivarianism is a mix of panhispanic, left-leaning and nationalist-patriotic ideals named after Simón Bolívar, the 19th-century Venezuelan general and liberator from the Spanish monarchy then in abeyance, who led the struggle for independence throughout much of South America.

Q216173.label: Free City of Danzig
Q216173.desc: semi-autonomous city-state that existed between 1920 and 1939
Q216173.summary: The Free City of Danzig was a city-state under the protection and oversight of the League of Nations between 1920 and 1939, consisting of the Baltic Sea port of Danzig and nearly 200 other small localities in the surrounding areas. The country was established on 15 November 1920, per the terms of Article 100 of the 1919 Treaty of Versailles, following the end of World War I.
